clue.text: Loutish behaviour of one with mullet perhaps on head

parts.note: the letter O looks like the figure for one
a mullet is an example of a fish, hence 'a fish'
a ness is a headland, a promontory jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A lout's behaviour is pinned on someone sporting a mullet haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mullet' suggests the haircut, which suits 'on head', but it is the fish; 'head' is a separate piece, the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish, clumsy conduct is what a lout shows, the quality of being an oaf.

clue.text: Doc came to be shaved by razor man

indicators.note: shaving trims the edges off, so the first and last letters of the phrase go and the run inside remains

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up to be given a shave by a barber.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters from DOCCAME to leave the philosopher's name.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Ockham gave his name to the principle of parsimony known as his razor.

clue.text: I'm surprised what woman wears at Ascot covering top of thighs

indicators.note: the hat is placed over another piece, so that piece goes inside it

parts.note: Royal Ascot, an English racing meeting, is famous for women's elaborate fancy hats

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here of thighs

explanation.surface: A racegoer's outfit at Ascot is somehow long enough to cover her thighs, to someone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses surprise, as one says 'well, well!'

clue.text: Football team not exactly brilliant, goals nil, all lost

indicators.note: the letters are not given exactly as printed but in a new order
lost says the letters of the word all go missing from the pool

explanation.surface: A football team's performance was hardly brilliant: no goals, and every match lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool BRILLIANT and GOALSNIL, take away the letters of ALL, and rearrange the rest; STIRLING ALBION is a Scottish league football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling Albion is a professional Scottish football club, an example of a team.

clue.text: This old sailor makes call to ship 'oy!'

clue.text: Chaplain's damaged main artery

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of the word before it are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A clergyman's principal blood vessel has suffered injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main artery' reads as anatomy, but 'main' is the sea and the artery a waterway; the 's of Chaplain's supplies the S here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship canal is a principal waterway for seagoing vessels, a transport artery.

clue.text: Miss out waste collector

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over, as when jumping a step
a large open container for rubbish, the British word for a dumpster

explanation.surface: A council's bin collection has been missed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over something is to omit it; a British dumpster for rubbish shares the name.

clue.text: Contemptible person turned up with oriental weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a fink is a contemptible person or informer
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A despicable character surfaced carrying an eastern blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade with a handle used for cutting or stabbing is a weapon.

clue.text: Having no port in, I ordered table wine

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lacking any port, a diner asks for an ordinary wine with the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a red grape variety and the everyday wine made from it.

clue.text: This business needs trade unions

parts.note: read as a firm dealing in unions between couples, a trade in weddings rather than labour organisations

explanation.surface: A company declares that it depends on organised labour.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent who arranges matches for a fee literally trades in matrimonial unions.

clue.text: Recycling actions in a lab in reusing old parts

indicators.note: recycling processes material into new forms, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A laboratory recycles its materials by salvaging old components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycling' looks like part of the definition but it is the anagram signal for the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking parts from one machine to repair another is stripping it for spares, the engineering sense of eating one's own kind.

clue.text: Insect might escape

parts.note: may is the present tense of might, as in 'may happen'
to fly is to flee or escape

explanation.surface: A bug may get away.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephemeral winged creature of rivers, famous for its short adult life.

clue.text: Film star exposed to wit Jonathan Ross let loose

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means to wit or namely

indicators.note: loose says the letters before it are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie star is exposed to the wit of the British chat-show host when he is let loose.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a British television presenter; his name and LET supply the anagram fodder after SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlett Johansson is an American actress, a Hollywood film star.

clue.text: See 12
Girl on vessel took in view, having travelled

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
an urn is a vessel
to have eyed something is to have taken it in view, looked at it

explanation.surface: A girl aboard a ship admired the scenery on her voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' wants to be a ship in this travel picture, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made a long trip is to have travelled, voyaged.

clue.text: Go through the motions with two things a minister has

parts.note: a British minister has a shadow, the opposition spokesman, and a red despatch box
a British minister has a shadow, the opposition spokesman, and a red despatch box

explanation.surface: Someone acts out a routine involving a pair of items a government official owns.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics each minister is shadowed by an opposition counterpart and carries papers in a red box.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar at an imaginary opponent is to make boxing movements without a fight.

clue.text: Name often found in nightclub eagerly anticipating Oscar

parts.note: agog means eagerly expectant
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A club-goer waits excitedly for an Oscar winner to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-go is a discotheque style, and the word often appears in nightclub names.

clue.text: A doctor's ordered a lot of shellfish

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are set into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the 's stands for 'is', supplying an S

explanation.surface: A doctor has prescribed a big helping of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a medical prescription; it is the anagram signal for ADOCTORS, with the second A added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracoda is a class of tiny bivalved crustaceans, a whole group of shelled creatures.

clue.text: Extremist contributing to awful tragedy

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fanatic played a part in a terrible disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a hardliner.

clue.text: Change engulfing City institution, one notwithstanding being split up

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing other letters inside

parts.note: to alter is to change
LSE, the London Stock Exchange, is in the City of London
a means one

explanation.surface: Reform swallows a financial institution, which keeps going despite being broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'notwithstanding' into 'not with standing' to see a stadium with seats for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium with seats for every spectator has no standing terraces.

clue.text: Not something read by PC? Yes it is

definitions.text: Not something read by PC? Yes it is

parts.note: taken as written
an e-book is a text read on a computer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an item is read on a computer and is told it is one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the joke: the portable computer is itself a PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop computer is a small portable PC.

clue.text: A tart turned up in US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means both pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tart is a slut, a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A prostitute surfaced in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Opening note penned by composer

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within the next piece, as in a pen

parts.note: J S Bach, the German composer
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A composer writes the first note of a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' and 'penned' suggest a written overture; it means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or hole, an opening in a wall.

clue.text: Countryman turning to say 'Oh dear'

indicators.note: turning says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
doh is the exclamation of annoyance made famous by Homer Simpson

explanation.surface: A rustic swings round to exclaim in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hodge is the traditional name for a typical English farm labourer, a rustic.

clue.text: Songstress keen to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: A singer is eager to make her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially of opera.

clue.text: Coward and one made of straw perhaps taken by girl here

definitions.text: Coward and one made of straw perhaps taken by girl here

parts.words: Coward and one made of straw perhaps taken by girl here
parts.note: in The Wizard of Oz Dorothy takes the Cowardly Lion and the Scarecrow along a famous route

explanation.surface: A cowardly man and a straw figure are led by a girl somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' suggests Noel Coward, but it is the Cowardly Lion; 'one made of straw' could be a brick, but it is the Scarecrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The path to the Emerald City in The Wizard of Oz is paved in golden-coloured bricks.

clue.text: Dull poet makes a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback here means the word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A boring poet returns to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dreary and colourless.

clue.text: Who's moving apart, exit to Spain?

definitions.text: Who's moving apart, exit to Spain?

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the words after it are shifted about

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A question about someone relocating abroad, leaving for Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines someone who has left their homeland to live abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant living outside their native country, like Britons on the Costa del Sol.
